Summary: TimeWarner reported a 76% jump in fourth‑quarter profit to $1.13 billion, helped by high‑speed internet sales and stronger advertising, while its film division saw a 27% profit decline. The media group now owns an 8% stake in Google, is facing an SEC investigation that will require restating past results, and plans to boost AOL subscriptions by offering the service free to its internet customers.
Organizations: TimeWarner, Google, AOL, Warner Bros, SEC, Bertelsmann

Summary: The dollar rose to its highest level against the euro in almost three months after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said the U.S. trade deficit is likely to stabilise, boosting confidence in the currency. The move follows a recent Fed rate hike and comes amid ongoing concerns about China’s pegged yuan and the upcoming U.S. budget announcement.
Organizations: Federal Reserve, Bank of America, G7, White House

Summary: Menatep Group, the owner of the embattled Russian oil company Yukos, will demand that state‑owned Rosneft repay a $900 million loan secured on the assets of the Yugansk production unit, which Rosneft bought for $9.3 billion after a forced sale. Rosneft already faces a similar $540 million repayment claim from foreign banks, and legal experts say the purchase obliges it to settle such debts, while Yukos alleges the sale was politically motivated.
People: Tim Osborne, Jamie Firestone, Mikhail Khodorkovsky
Organizations: Yukos, Menatep Group, Rosneft, Yugansk

Summary: British Airways reported a 40% fall in pre‑tax profit for the quarter to 31 December 2004, blaming a sharp rise in fuel costs and noting that fuel surcharges only partially offset the increase. Despite the profit dip, turnover grew, cargo revenue improved and the airline expects slightly better full‑year revenue than previously forecast, while warning of lower passenger yields amid competition.
People: Rod Eddington, Martin Broughton, Mike Powell, Nick Van den Brul
Organizations: British Airways, Dresdner Kleinwort Wasserstein, BNP Paribas

Summary: Shares in UK drinks and food group Allied Domecq rose after reports that French spirits company Pernod Ricard may be considering a takeover bid, though no formal approach has been made. Both firms, valued at roughly €8‑9 billion, have been highlighted as potential consolidation targets following recent portfolio improvements and debt reductions.
Organizations: Allied Domecq, Pernod Ricard, Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, Seagram, Diageo, Glenmorangie, LVMH
Locations: United Kingdom, France, London, Paris, Scotland

Summary: Japan's economy grew only 0.1% in the third quarter, following a similar contraction in the previous quarter, putting it on the brink of a technical recession with annual growth of just 0.2%. While the government downplayed the outlook, economists warned that a stronger yen and weak domestic demand make the recovery appear patchier than previously thought.
Organizations: Japanese government, Lehman Brothers

Summary: US firms added 146,000 jobs in January, falling short of the 190,000 expected, but the drop in jobseekers pushed the unemployment rate down to 5.2%, the lowest since September 2001. The Labor Department also revised December's job gains downward, and economists said the pace of employment growth remains moderate despite favorable economic conditions.
People: President Bush, Rick Egelton, Ken Mayland, Herbert Hoover
Organizations: Labor Department, BMO Financial Group, ClearView Economics

Summary: India's finance minister Palaniappan Chidambaram criticised G7 nations' trade policies and called for reforms of the UN, World Bank and IMF ahead of the G7 summit in London, arguing for more flexible exchange rates and fairer terms of globalisation. He attended the meeting as part of the G20 delegation, while the IMF warned that India's large budget deficit could hinder growth projected at about 6.5% for the year to March 2005.
Organizations: G7, G20, United Nations, World Bank, International Monetary Fund
Locations: London, India, China, Brazil, South Africa, Russia, United States

Summary: Ethiopia's crop output rose to 14.27 million tonnes in 2004, a 24% increase from the previous year, driven by good rains, more fertilizer use and improved seeds, according to a joint FAO‑WFP report. Despite the boost, 2.2 million people still require emergency aid, and the FAO recommends sourcing food assistance locally to support domestic markets.
Organizations: Food and Agriculture Organisation, World Food Programme

Summary: A US appeals court dismissed the government’s $280 billion lawsuit against major tobacco firms, ruling it could not be pursued under anti‑racketeering statutes. The case, filed by the Clinton administration in 1999, alleged the companies concealed smoking harms and targeted youth, but the firms cite a prior $206 billion settlement with states. Shares of the tobacco companies rose after the decision.
Organizations: US government, Clinton administration, Altria Group, RJ Reynolds Tobacco, Lorillard Tobacco, Liggett Group, Brown and Williamson, Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia
Locations: Washington, District of Columbia, United States

Summary: Ask Jeeves reported a near‑tripling of revenue to $86 million and a $17 million profit in Q4 2004, positioning it as the third‑largest online search firm after Google and Yahoo. The rise reflects a broader rebound in internet advertising, also boosting Doubleclick’s profits, though shares of both Ask Jeeves and Doubleclick fell about 4 % due to high investor expectations.
Organizations: Ask Jeeves, Google, Yahoo, Doubleclick

Summary: Indonesia's government is weighing a fuel price increase of up to 30% to curb costly subsidies and redirect funds to poverty aid, a move championed by President Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono and State Minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati. Critics warn the hike could hurt low‑income families, and past attempts to cut subsidies have sparked public protests.
People: Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono, Sri Mulyani Indrawati, Rachel Harvey, Megawati Sukarnoputri
Organizations: Indonesian government, BBC

Summary: Mitsubishi Motors has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Peugeot to supply 30,000 SUVs built in Japan using Peugeot diesel engines, with a final agreement expected by spring 2005. The deal is intended to utilise Mitsubishi’s underused capacity and provide a financial boost as the company faces steep sales declines, profit warnings and seeks additional funding.
Organizations: Mitsubishi Motors, Peugeot, DaimlerChrysler, Nissan Motor, Mitsubishi Group

Summary: The Daily and Sunday Telegraph will cut 90 journalist positions, about 17% of their editorial staff, to fund a £150 million investment in new printing facilities. The National Union of Journalists has condemned the move, calling for a recall of the redundancy notices and warning of possible strike action. The cuts come as the Telegraph Group, owned by the Barclay twins, seeks to improve production capability amid industry-wide competition and declining revenues.
People: Jeremy Dear, Barry Fitzpatrick, Frederick Barclay, David Barclay, Murdoch MacLennan, Conrad Black
Organizations: Daily Telegraph, Sunday Telegraph, Telegraph Group, National Union of Journalists, Pearson Financial Times, Littlewoods, News Corp, News International, The Sun, News of the World, Guardian Media Group, Trinity Mirror, Daily Mail & General Trust

Summary: The EU has introduced new rules requiring airlines to pay compensation of €250‑€600 for overbooking, cancellations or delays, applying to all scheduled and charter flights. The legislation faces legal challenges from the European Low‑fare Airlines Association and IATA, while airlines and industry groups argue it will raise ticket prices for passengers.
People: Michael Cawley, Andy Clarke, Marja Quillinan‑Meiland, Jacques Barrot
Organizations: European Commission, European Low‑fare Airlines Association (ELAA), International Air Transport Association (IATA), European Regions Airline Association (ERAA), Ryanair

Summary: China will maintain credit restrictions into 2005 to prevent overheating, after introducing curbs earlier this year to curb inflation and protect its banking system. Despite a 9.1% growth rate and strong corporate investment, the government aims to keep growth around its 7% target while managing a cheap yuan peg and high energy demand that has lifted global oil prices.
Organizations: Chinese government, state media

Summary: Parmalat announced that its fourth‑quarter pre‑tax profit doubled to €77 million, while also being fined €11 million for breaching takeover rules. The company, still burdened by roughly €12 billion of debt, is pursuing extensive legal action, including a lawsuit by administrator Enrico Bondi against former banker Morgan Stanley to recover €136 million.
Organizations: Parmalat, Morgan Stanley

Summary: India's rupee rose to a five‑year high after Standard & Poor's upgraded the country's foreign‑currency rating to BB+, one notch below investment grade. The rating boost is expected to attract foreign capital back to Indian markets, reversing recent outflows to places like Korea and Thailand. Strategist Bhanu Baweja of UBS said the upgrade will serve as an incentive for investors to return to India.
Organizations: Standard & Poor's, UBS
Locations: India, Korea, Thailand, Romania, Egypt, El Salvador, Russia

Summary: India has increased the foreign direct investment ceiling in telecom companies from 49% to 74% to attract the $20 billion needed for rapid mobile market growth, aiming to boost mobile users to 200‑250 million by 2007. The move, announced by Communications Minister Dayanidhi Maran, requires government approval for stakes above 49% and mandates senior executive roles be held by Indians, drawing praise from analysts and investors.
People: Dayanidhi Maran, Manmohan Singh, Kobita Desai, Sanjay Mehta
Organizations: Government of India, Gartner, Ernst & Young, Morgan Stanley, Bharti Televentures, Singapore Telecom, Essar, Hutchison Whampoa, Sterling Group, Tata Group

Summary: A survey commissioned by Dimension Data found that callers now abandon calls after an average of 65 seconds, with abandonment rates rising to 13.3% and training time for agents falling from 36 to 21 days. The study links reduced patience to mobile usage and expanding call‑centre responsibilities, while noting that offshoring is not the primary driver of poor performance.
Organizations: Dimension Data, Sunovate
Locations: India, South Africa, Europe, North America

Summary: Leisure group Rank is considering demerging its Deluxe Film unit, valued at about £300 million, and selling its media business, with details to be disclosed alongside its financial results on Friday. The move follows a cost‑cutting programme since CEO Mike Smith took charge in 1999, leaving the company focused on gaming, bars and hotels, including its Hard Rock brand. Analysts expect a slight dip in pre‑tax profit for the year.
Organizations: Rank, Goldman Sachs, Deluxe Film, Deluxe Media, Hard Rock, Odeon, Pinewood Studios, Mecca Bingo, Grosvenor Casinos

Summary: German unemployment rose for the tenth consecutive month in November, reaching 4.464 million people (10.8% of the workforce), as sluggish growth and high oil prices weigh on the labour market. The government, led by Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder, is implementing controversial job‑creation measures such as “one‑euro jobs,” while officials say modest domestic demand improvements are insufficient to reverse the trend.
People: Frank-Juergen Weise, Gerhard Schroeder, Isabelle Kronawitter
Organizations: Federal Labour Agency, Hypovereinsbank

Summary: France’s economy accelerated in the final quarter of 2004, with a seasonally‑adjusted growth of 0.7‑0.8% and annual GDP up 2.3%, though still below the government’s 2.5% target. Industrial output rose 0.7% in December and service activity hit a seven‑month high, while unemployment remained around 10%, prompting optimism from officials and economists for continued improvement into 2005.
Organizations: INSEE, French government, European Central Bank, Deutsche Bank

Summary: The United States recorded an all‑time trade deficit of $671.7 billion in 2004, with imports outpacing exports and the gap with China reaching a record $162 billion. Democrats criticized President Bush’s economic policies and China’s currency practices, while the administration and some economists argued the deficit reflects strong domestic growth and may even boost Q4 growth estimates.
Organizations: US Commerce Department, IXIS

Summary: A Texas judge dismissed Yukos's attempt to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US, ruling the company lacks sufficient US presence to establish jurisdiction. The decision hampers Yukos's efforts to challenge the Russian‑state auction of its Yugansk oil division, while former Yukos chief Mikhail Khodorkovsky began his fraud and tax‑evasion trial in Russia.
People: Mikhail Khodorkovsky, Letitia Clark, Bruce Misamore, Steven Theede
Organizations: Yukos, Rosneft, Gazpromneft, Gazprom, Deutsche Bank

Summary: General Motors is recalling nearly 200,000 vehicles in the United States due to potential brake system failures and other safety defects, including issues with accelerator pedals and windshields. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration warned that the faults could lead to crashes, though GM reports no injuries so far. The recall comes as GM anticipates lower earnings this year amid weak sales and other financial pressures.
Organizations: General Motors, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac, Pontiac, Buick, Isuzu
